lines.t: Why do over a million people play Counter-Strike 2 every single day?
It is five against five. One team plants a bomb, the other team stops them, and there are no respawns.
Every round you earn money, and spend it on weapons for the next one.

sc.label: EVERY ROUND
sc.sub: win rounds, earn cash, buy better guns

lines.t: It started in 1999 as a fan mod for Half-Life, made by Minh Le and Jess Cliffe. Valve picked it up a year later.
In April 2025 it hit its all-time record: 1.86 million players at the same time.
Pro tournaments fill entire arenas. This year's Cologne Major peaked at 2.75 million viewers.
The weapon skins are worth real money. One rifle skin reportedly sold for over a million dollars.
Trackers put the whole skin market at around 6 billion dollars.
One update last October reportedly wiped two billion dollars off that market in a single day.
Fun detail: bullets and grenades punch real holes in smoke clouds.
And Steam still says it came out in 2012, because it took over the old game's store page.
It's free, simple to understand, and almost impossible to master.
